title: Continuous cocycles and the completed augmentation resolution
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $G$ a profinite group, and $M$ a discrete $\Lambda$-module with continuous $\Lambda$-linear $G$-action [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. Define $A=\Lambda[[G]]=\varprojlim_{U\trianglelefteq_o G}\Lambda[G/U]$, with augmentation $\epsilon:A\to\Lambda$ summing coefficients, and put $I=\ker\epsilon$. Write $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,\mathrm{cont}}(I,M)$ for continuous $A$-linear maps, with $I$ carrying its subspace topology. A continuous crossed homomorphism is a continuous map $c:G\to M$ with $c(gh)=c(g)+g c(h)$; its coboundaries are $c_m(g)=gm-m$. Then there is a natural isomorphism
$$H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{A,\mathrm{cont}}(I,M)\big/\{a\mapsto am:m\in M\},$$
which sends the class of $c$ to the class of the unique continuous $A$-linear map $f_c$ satisfying $f_c(g-1)=c(g)$ for every $g\in G$. This is the comparison with the augmented resolution $0\to I\to A\to\Lambda\to0$; in particular, whenever this resolution is used to compute degree one, it is this comparison, not its negative. If $\sigma$ topologically generates $G$ and $A\to I$, $a\mapsto a(1-\sigma)$, is a topological $A$-module isomorphism, all $A$-linear maps $I\to M$ are continuous and the same comparison identifies degree one with the cokernel of $M\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(I,M)$, $m\mapsto(a\mapsto am)$. In these coordinates
$$f_c(1-\sigma)=-c(\sigma).$$
